_note: Calibrated at GRAND_OFFERS=25 with the batcher at 7 slots; enforcement is baseline x 1.2. Wall-clock numbers — re-calibrate for a different scale or box, and note publishToIndexed is dominated by the celestia delayMs, not by node work. sseDeliveryLagP50Ms/P95Ms are ABSENT on purpose: the metric was redefined and its baseline must be re-derived from measurement rather than carried over. It used to mix two populations — CONSUMED archives (event-driven, where the archiving block IS the spending block, so the gap really is block -> STM -> event bus -> socket) and TTL archives (performed by a SCHEDULED input, whose archived_at is a block timestamp the STM may not reach until much later while catching up from the storm). At ~40% TTL (14 of 35), that second population's variance swamped the first: p95 read 2674, then 6899, then 23572 across three runs while maxStmLagBlocks went DOWN (95 -> 83) and both throughput metrics improved. Two different things in one number, and the noisy one winning. p7b now gates CONSUMED archives only and reports the TTL population as a note; STM scheduling latency is already gated by maxStmLagBlocks. Populate these two keys from the next clean run. bookReadP95Ms raised 10 -> 20 earlier for a related reason: at count=10 the p95 IS the max, and one 19ms read (median unmoved at 7-8ms) tripped the gate. A real regression moves the median. maxStmLagBlocks 89 -> 95: the suite publishes ~10 more offers and runs an extra phase, so the storm's catch-up peak is genuinely deeper — a load-profile change, not a node regression. bookRead is now gated on the MEDIAN (bookReadP50Ms), not the tail: it collects 10 samples, at which point p95 IS max, so one slow read defined the gate. That fired three times with the median unmoved at 7-8ms, and raising the threshold each time was measuring nothing. bookReadP95Ms is retained but only ENFORCED at >= 50 samples (MIN_TAIL_SAMPLES); below that it is reported as a note. Same rule now applies to sseDeliveryLagP95Ms. submitP95Ms and publishToIndexedP95Ms share the low-count property (~29 and ~33 samples) and are still gated on p95 alone - they pass today, so tightening them is a separate change, but they should gain p50 baselines at the next recalibration.
